implementation_notes: F7d = Amendment 7's M2 leave-self-out (LSO) variant, fixing the M1 defect: every candidate known at origin o (positive & date<origin, primary/unshifted definition) was, in F7, itself a member of K3(o) and (if it supplied the formula's GPR training point) of the GPR training set -- so its own dist collapsed to 0 and its posterior sigma sat near its floor, values no genuinely-unknown test candidate could ever have. M2: for each such candidate, individually, its own raw-id contribution (all distance-anchor points AND, if applicable, its 9 synthetic training points) is removed from K3(o)/the GPR training set, the GPR is refit by maximum likelihood on the reduced set, and its own dist/logcd/sigma are recomputed against that reduced K3(o) -- one candidate at a time, so every OTHER known candidate's points (including their exact fixed noise draws) are left untouched in each such refit. Candidates NOT known at an origin are completely unchanged from F7's own features_recomputed.csv (verified, see below).

Every 'known positive' candidate maps, by construction, to >=1 raw id in a matched-detection record (step2_build_candidates.py: positive = any member matched to a post2021 detection via rules A/B/C) -- the 87 Lee Table A2 anchors were already purged out of the raw universe by F6's Rule A and so can never themselves be a 'known positive candidate'; LSO removal targets only a candidate's own raw-id points, never anchor points.

Step 1 check (candidates NOT known at each origin vs F7's features_recomputed.csv, tolerance 1e-9): True -- 5651 rows checked, max abs diff 1.776e-15 (machine precision). Full report: step1_not_known_check.json.

109 individual LOO refits performed across the 4 origins (16, 25, 30, 38 known candidates at origins 2022-01-01 through 2025-01-01 respectively) -- one independent GPR refit per known candidate, per origin. Full per-refit log (candidate_id, species_key, points removed, resulting training-set size, LML): loo_refit_log.json.

step4_engine.py's run_origin_evaluation(cand, Xs, sensitivity) evaluates all 4 ORIGINS against ONE fixed feature snapshot; F7d's features are origin-varying (like F7's), so it was called once per origin and only the matching origin's own result kept -- same per-origin-extraction pattern as F7's own step3_seal_results_f7.py. All evaluation logic itself (step4_engine.py, step5_bootstrap.py, j2_shift.py) is imported completely unmodified.

No pass/fail verdicts are computed in this file -- point estimates, pooled sums and bootstrap intervals only, matching F4a/F4c/F6/F7's convention. Per Amendment 7's M3, this is a post hoc correction to F7 (fixing a defect M1 identified after F7 was unsealed), labelled as such, and is never used to silently replace F7's pre-registered sealed result -- both sealed files stand on their own.
